title: Mouse Highlighter conflicting with highlight mode : Ripple
author: xapollyon
summary: A current mainline Mouse Highlighter change addresses the class of lost-button-up and stale ripple/pressed-state failures described by the report.

status.label: Covered by current mainline fix
status.detail: The low-level hook and lifecycle state handling were changed to prevent ripple state remaining stuck.

next_action.label: Verify in a released build
next_action.reason: The issue predates the mainline fix; confirm the reporter's stable channel contains it before closing.

judgment.rationale: The report describes a stale visual state after switching to Ripple. Commit dbff0e79 changes Mouse Highlighter's hook/event queue, button-up preservation, settings transitions, and teardown cleanup specifically to prevent ripple or pressed state becoming stuck. The exact reporter sequence remains absent, so release verification is still needed.
evidence: The issue reports a circle remaining at its last position after choosing Ripple mode.
MouseHighlighter.cpp contains ClearDrawing, ProcessPendingSettings, and MouseHighlighterSwitch lifecycle paths.
Mainline commit dbff0e79 documents that a lost button-up in the low-level hook could leave ripple or pressed state stuck and resets transient visual state during stop, settings changes, and teardown.
The commit also marshals Composition work and settings application away from the low-level hook, directly addressing the relevant state/lifetime failure class.
No reporter reply or exact transition sequence is available to prove which branch was hit.
judgment.recommended_action: Verify the behavior in a build containing dbff0e79; if it still reproduces, collect the exact activation and mode-switch sequence before designing another fix.

fix_assessment.rationale: An existing mainline change covers the suspected stuck ripple/pressed-state mechanism and lifecycle cleanup.

issue_context.summary: Mouse Highlighter can leave a circle visible after the user switches to Ripple mode.

issue_context.analysis: Because a concrete merged mainline change covers the relevant failure mechanism, a competing proposed fix would be misleading. The remaining work is release/version confirmation, not speculative redesign.
